current_bottleneck: The accepted MVP used a coordinator-side clear order and seven party processes on one host rather than participant-edge sharing into node-local custody.
causal_hypothesis: Direct participant-to-node VSS delivery plus one isolated party executor per node will preserve the expected 40-lot match while removing the complete order from coordinator memory.
single_intended_change: Replace coordinator-side Shamir dealing in the distributed acceptance path with signed edge manifests, seven encrypted node-specific shares, and node-signed idempotent execution receipts.
baseline: The release gate matches and settles correctly, but its MpcRunner receives the complete private order before generating party files.
most_likely_prediction_error: MP-SPDZ process startup and the heavily loaded single OmenX host may push elapsed time above 15000 ms without changing the functional result.
rejection_rules: either participant receives fewer than seven node acknowledgements
any node accepts a share addressed to another party
the coordinator receives a complete order or all seven shares
the seven malicious-shamir parties do not agree
trade price is not 100 or quantity is not 40
the same signed round causes another execution
the artifact claims independent operators or live Avalanche settlement
promotion_rules: every functional rejection rule remains false
a fresh machine-readable artifact binds the topology, code digests, node receipts and result
the artifact explicitly records one operator host and no live Avalanche claim
